stem: A nurse educator is selecting a preceptor for a newly licensed nurse entering a transition-to-practice program. Which preparation is specifically supported by NCSBN study findings?

options.A: Use a preceptor who has been educated for the preceptor role
options.B: Assign any available nurse without role preparation
options.C: Avoid preceptorship because it delays independent practice
options.D: Use only self-study modules and eliminate direct preceptor feedback

rationale: NCSBN's national Transition to Practice study found significantly better outcomes when transition programs included a preceptorship and the preceptor was educated for that role. Availability or years of practice alone do not substitute for preparation to function effectively as a preceptor.
educational_objective: Recognize NCSBN-supported preparation of preceptors in transition-to-practice programs.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Phase I: program characteristic — a preceptorship, and the preceptor should be educated for the role
source_claim_supported: Supports use of a preceptorship with a preceptor educated for the role.
correction_summary: Replaced unsupported broad selection traits with the specific preceptor preparation supported by NCSBN study findings.
audit_findings: A is the only option directly supported by NCSBN; B-D contradict the study model.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
